chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb: that he asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about the best thing by which the servants draw near to their Lord, so he said:
"I do not know of anything, after ma'rifah, better than salat (prayer)."

key_terms.أَفْضَلِ: best; greatest in merit and excellence
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer); the foremost devotional act after ma'rifah
key_terms.الْعِبَادُ: the servants; human beings in their relation of servitude to Allah
key_terms.الْمَعْرِفَةِ: ma'rifah; true recognition and knowledge of Allah and divine truth
key_terms.رَبِّهِمْ: their Lord; Allah as the nurturer and master of His servants
key_terms.يَتَقَرَّبُ: draws near; seeks nearness to Allah through worship

ai.seo_question: What is the best act after ma'rifah for drawing near to Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that after ma'rifah, salat (prayer) is the greatest act by which a servant draws near to Allah. It highlights the supreme spiritual rank of prayer within the life of faith and worship.
